history.summary: Brahmeshwar Nath at Brahmpur village (Buxar district) is an ancient Shiva temple famous for its swayambhu (self-originated) Shivling and its unusual west-facing entrance - all other Shiva temples being east-facing. Legend holds that Brahma himself established the linga, and that when the invader Ghaznavi challenged the deity to turn the temple door from east to west overnight, the door indeed faced west the next morning and the temple was spared. The Rudra Samhita of the Shiva Mahapurana is cited as granting the linga's devotees Dharma, Artha, Kama and Moksha - hence Manokamna Mahadev. CSV ERRORS: the CSV 'state' column holds the town name 'Buxar'; the real state is Bihar. Also the CSV town 'Buxar' is approximate: the temple is at Brahmpur village ~33 km from Buxar town (one source). Construction-date claims conflict (Gupta period vs unknown) and the pre-1764 British-visit story is weakly sourced - both flagged.

name: Brahmeshwar Nath Temple
town_description: Brahmpur is a large village and block in Buxar district of Bihar, about 33 km from Buxar town. Its name means 'the place of Brahma', and it is known for the west-facing Brahmeshwar Nath Shiva temple and a large cattle fair that draws visitors from across Bihar and eastern Uttar Pradesh.
